extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A public open-source dataset of non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes paired with corresponding radiology text reports, with abnormality labels extracted from reports and additional anatomical segmentation labels.
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Chenyu Wang, Furkan Almas, Ayse Gulnihan Simsek, Sewal Nil Esirgun, Irem Dogan, Omer Faruk Durugol, Benjamin Hou, Suprosanna Shit, Weicheng Dai, Murong Xu, Hadrien Reynaud, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Bastian Wittmann, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Enis Simsar, Mehmet Simsar, Emine Bensu Erdemir, Abdullah Alanbay, Anjany Sekuboyina, Berkan Lafci, Ahmet Kaplan, Zhiyong Lu, Malgorzata Polacin, Bernhard Kainz, Christian Bluethgen, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, Bjoern Menze
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology reports were curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes all reconstructed non-contrast chest CT volumes from the hospital database within the stated period, with reports anonymized, translated to English, reviewed by bilingual final-year medical students, and CT volumes filtered to exclude contrast studies and non-chest body parts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consist of chest CT volumes, associated metadata, and radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital hospital database.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing personal information with regular expressions, translated from Turkish to English using Google Translate API, then reviewed and corrected by bilingual final-year medical students. CT metadata were anonymized and orientations standardized. For label creation, findings and impression sections were merged, some related conditions were grouped under shared abnormality categories, and absent mentions were treated as absent.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Volumes with contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded. Each CT volume orientation was standardized, resized to 0.75 mm x/y and 1.5 mm z spacing, center-cropped or padded to 480×480×240, converted to Hounsfield Units using intercept and slope metadata, clipped to [-1000, 1000], and normalized to [-1, 1] during training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Radiology reports authored by radiologists accompany each scan. For abnormality labels, 1,000 reports were manually annotated for 18 abnormalities after merging findings and impression sections; a RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model was then fine-tuned on these annotations and applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels were generated using a state-of-the-art segmentation model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The automated report classifier's precision, recall, and F1 scores were evaluated and reported, indicating robust classification across abnormalities.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 radiology report per scan; manual abnormality annotation was performed on 1,000 reports
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Radiologists authored the reports; bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected translations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google Translate API; RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m; automated text classifier; state-of-the-art segmentation model; TotalSegmentator
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan future extensions to CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels; current releases include raw data, preprocessing scripts, and anatomical segmentation labels via the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age, sex, patient symptoms and medical history, scan metadata, and radiology reports originally containing patient and medical professional identifiers; reports were originally in Turkish and translated to English.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and derived models are intended to address critical challenges in 3D medical imaging, support future innovations in medical AI, improve patient care, reduce radiologists' workload, and broaden accessibility through a user-friendly interface for educational and clinical research settings.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is single-institution and from a single geographic and clinical setting, which may bias self-supervised training and limit generalizability to other populations. Detection performance also depends on report terminology and prompt choice.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: CT-RATE is a single-center dataset, which may limit generalizability. Current models are limited to chest CT volumes. Benchmarking for CT-CHAT is constrained by the lack of pretrained 3D multimodal baselines. Generated reports remain insufficient for clinical use, and the systems are far from ready for clinical deployment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and internal validation of CT-CLIP and CT-CHAT; validation and fine-tuning for multi-abnormality detection; zero-shot detection; volume-to-volume and report-to-volume retrieval; visual question answering; radiology report generation; visual grounding and anatomical localization support via segmentation labels.
